== Research Notes ==

A possible identification concerns John Glasgow, Loughinsholin freeholder, 1831. The 16 August 1831 declaration lists Robert Glasgow and John Glasgow among freeholders of the barony printed Loughinshollen (modern Loughinsholin), County Londonderry, supporting Sir Robert Bateson. They are co-signatories; no kinship, occupation, age or individual townland is given. Castledawson and 4 July 1831 refer to the opposing meeting discussed in the declaration, not their homes or their signing date.<ref>Belfast News-Letter, 16 August 1831, p.3, Loughinshollen freeholders’ declaration; [https://www.newspapers.com/image/390548642/ record].</ref> [[Glasgow-2058]], [[Glasgow-3927]] (an indexed freeholder with uncertain locality), [[Glasgow-2990]] and [[Glasgow-4090]] remain adult regional comparisons. No same-name co-signature establishes descent, brotherhood or identity with the Cookstown merchant. The declaration concerns a holding in the barony, not necessarily residence there. The identification remains uncertain.
